title: throughput-aware-token-coalescer-and-on-the-fly-dequant-fusion
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Continuous batching and streaming workloads exposed a recurring tradeoff between peak throughput and tail latency when serving quantized models. Existing dequant fusion paths reduced copies but were brittle under token-coalescing alignment and caused KV cache churn for long-prefix streaming sessions. This PR introduces a throughput-aware token coalescer that aligns microbatches with runtime kernel characteristics, plus an on-the-fly dequant fusion path that avoids re-materializing large dequant buffers for many streaming tokens. Summary: 1) Token coalescer: a scheduler module that groups pending generation requests by expected token-length distribution and per-request latency SLO hint; it produces microbatches aligned to kernel-friendly widths to improve GEMM throughput and cache locality. 2) Streaming dequant fusion: new kernel-side fusion that performs dequantization only for the head projection necessary for next-token logits and keeps remainder in-place as quantized until needed. This reduces memory traffic and amortizes dequant cost across coalesced tokens. 3) KV cache checkpointing and prefix-hinting: a small metadata extension to the KV cache that allows the runtime to detect prefix reuse across streaming requests and avoid redundant KV reconstructions when coalescer rearranges order. 4) Runtime flags and per-model hints: allow safe rollback and A/B rollout for dedicated hosts. Key metrics: - INT8 T5-like model, synthetic throughput benchmark (perf-canary): +1.35x overall throughput at stable load when coalescer enabled. - p50 latency improved by 18% and p95 improved by 12% under mixed short/long request distributions. - Memory bandwidth reduction observed (~34% less DDR transfers during sustained streaming compared to previous dequant path). Safety & compatibility: this introduces no change to public API; behavior is behind config flags in model config and runtime config (runtime.experimental.token_coalescer, model.quant.dequant_fusion=on_the_fly). Default rollout is off for hosted tier; enabled by default on dedicated experimental fleets. Tests & validation: unit tests for coalescer logic, kernel microbench harness for fused dequant path, integration tests exercising KV prefix reuse during continuous batching, perf-canary jobs with representative traces. Migration & rollout: - Start with canary hosts using dedicated capacity (A/B). - Observe cost and latency metrics for 72h before wider rollout. - Revert path: turn off runtime.experimental.token_coalescer and model hint. Related: follows design notes in ENG-1298 and leverages kernel helpers introduced in ENG-1330. Links: perf-canary job: perf-canary/job/2026-02-20/ta-coalescer. Checklist: - [x] Token coalescer scheduler implementation - [x] Kernel-side on-the-fly dequant fusion - [x] KV prefix-hint metadata and checkpointing - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary and benchmark results attached - [x] Docs for ops toggles and rollback plan - [x] Feature flags gated for hosted/dedicated tiers Known issues and future work: - Small throughput regression observed for extremely short (<2 tokens) single-token hot paths; will add fast-path bypass in follow-up. - FP8 paths unchanged in this PR; follow-up will implement analogous fusion for FP8 quantized models. Implementation notes: coalescer uses a lightweight cost model derived from observed kernel throughput and selects microbatch widths that minimize expected per-token wall time. Dequant fusion uses a two-stage kernel: head-dequant + remainder-lazy. Both changes are conservative: when a model or host reports incompatibility, runtime falls back to the previous stable path.

release_notes: Improved INT8 inference throughput and streaming latency by introducing a throughput-aware token coalescer and an on-the-fly dequant fusion kernel. Adds KV cache prefix-hinting to avoid redundant KV reconstructions during continuous batching. Experimental behind feature flags; rollout plan included.
